description:
Replace HEEx-style template syntax with JSX-flavored Elixir. No <%= %> control flow, no @foo sigil, no EEx delimiters. All expressions are plain Elixir locals. Component invocation is via module alias.

READ FIRST:
- lib/filament/tag_engine.ex      (forked engine from T1 — parser lives here)
- lib/filament/html_engine.ex     (classify_type/1 determines how a tag is handled)
- examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_list.ex   (primary migration target)
- examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/filter_bar.ex
- examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_item.ex

SYNTAX CHANGES — exactly what must work in ~F templates:

1. TEXT INTERPOLATION
   Old: {@variable}  and  <%= expr %>  (both forms exist today)
   New: {variable}  and  {expr}       (bare Elixir expression, no @)
   Note: {expr} interpolation inside element content already works in HEEx;
   remove any special handling that requires @ prefix.

2. CONTROL FLOW BLOCKS
   Old: <%= if cond do %> … <% else %> … <% end %>
   New: {if cond do} … {else} … {end}

   Old: <%= for x <- list do %> … <% end %>
   New: {for x <- list do} … {end}   (Comprehension — see T4 for struct emit)

   The parser must accept bare Elixir block keywords (if/for/case/cond/with)
   wrapped in { } as block delimiters. {end} closes the block. {else}/{rescue}/
   {catch}/{after} are clause separators.

3. COMPONENT INVOCATION
   Old: <%= MyModule.render(%{prop: val, other: val2}) %>
   New: <MyModule prop={val} other={val2} />   (self-closing)
        <MyModule prop={val}>…children…</MyModule>  (with children, future)

   classify_type/1 in Filament.HTMLEngine must identify capitalized tag names
   (or dotted names like Alias.Name) as components rather than HTML elements.
   The generated call is: MyModule.render(%{prop: val, other: val2}).

   The module name in the tag must be resolvable at compile time via the aliases
   in the caller's __ENV__. Use Macro.expand({:__aliases__, [], parts}, caller_env)
   to resolve the alias to a full module name.

   Component calls must be hoisted by the hoist_dynamics pass (T2) — they are
   child renders that must run in the active render context, not inside the
   dynamic fn closure.

MIGRATION — update all example components to use new syntax:

examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_list.ex:
  Replace: <%= if todos != [] do %> … <% end %>
  With:    {if todos != [] do} … {end}

  Replace: <%= for todo <- filtered do %> … <% end %>
  With:    {for todo <- filtered do} … {end}

  Replace: <%= TodoItem.render(%{todo: todo, on_toggle: fn -> … end, on_remove: fn -> … end}) %>
  With:    <TodoItem todo={todo} on_toggle={fn -> … end} on_remove={fn -> … end} />

  Replace: <%= filter_bar %>
  With:    {filter_bar}
  (filter_bar is a local variable holding a %Rendered{} — bare interpolation)

examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/filter_bar.ex:
  Replace: <%= for {{value, label}, handler} <- Enum.zip(filters, handlers) do %> … <% end %>
  With:    {for {{value, label}, handler} <- Enum.zip(filters, handlers) do} … {end}

examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_item.ex:
  No control flow — no changes to template syntax needed (already uses {expr} form).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- In Filament.TagEngine, find where EEx tag delimiters (<% %>) are parsed and
  add support for the { } block syntax. Phoenix's HEEx already supports {expr}
  for interpolation — extend to support block forms.
- If the TagEngine's parser is too difficult to extend for block syntax, an
  alternative is to preprocess the source string in VNodeCompiler.compile/2 before
  passing to the engine: transform {if cond do}…{end} → <%= if cond do %>…<% end %>
  as a source-level rewrite. This is simpler and acceptable for this ticket.
- For classify_type/1: a tag starting with an uppercase letter or containing a
  dot is a component. Return :remote_component or the equivalent type that causes
  the engine to emit a function call rather than an HTML tag.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `mix test` passes
- All three example components use new syntax (no <%= %> in templates)
- Chrome: localhost:4000 — add todos (tests interpolation), toggle (tests event handlers),
  filter All/Active/Completed (tests for-loop, component invocation, if block)
- Specifically: clicking Active shows only uncompleted todos; clicking Completed shows
  only completed todos — this exercises the {for} loop and {if} block paths
title: JSX syntax in ~F: bare {expr} interpolation, {if/for do}…{end} blocks, <Module /> component calls
